gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on 2026-11-10 the Sony PS-LX3BT costs $399.99 at Turntable Lab and $398 at WorldWide Stereo, not the $349.99 ChatGPT showed. For $379, $21 less, Turntable Lab's Audio-Technica AT-LP3XBT is also fully automatic with aptX Bluetooth, and it adds an adjustable counterweight, anti-skate and a removable headshell with a VM95C cartridge. Turntable Lab lists none of those three for the Sony.
standout_why: I compared against turntableverse.com (opened 2026-11-10). It prices five models: PS-LX3BT at $349.99 on sale with a $399.99 list, LP70XBT $299, Pro-Ject E1 BT $499, LP120XBT-USB $449 and PS-LX310BT $449.99. It does not list the AT-LP3XBT, the Kanto OBI3 Gen 2 or the Sony PS-LX5BT, and it has no price check from today. The What Hi-Fi pages (cited), both Louder pages (one cited) and TechRadar returned only their headlines through the fetch tool, and vinylpickup.com failed with a certificate error. So I can't rule out that those pages list the LP3XBT. ChatGPT's own answers left it out in both chats.
decides: This confirms the AT-LP70XBT ($299) as the default automatic pick: it costs $100 less than the PS-LX3BT at both US specialist retailers I checked today, and turntableverse lists aptX Adaptive for both. It also weakens ChatGPT's 'best for easy operation' Sony slot. At $398–$399.99 today the Sony costs more than the AT-LP3XBT ($379), which is also one-button automatic but has a tonearm the buyer can adjust and upgrade. Under $260, the Kanto OBI3 Gen 2 ($249.99) undercuts the black LP60XBT ($259) if the buyer accepts semi-automatic operation.
